=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:46-63 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The shell renderer only performs exact whole-line matches for three legacy placeholders, so the new continuation variables and inline `{{VAR}}` tokens pass through unresolved.
  WHY: That breaks the conflict-resolver continuation prompt at runtime because `render_conflict_thread_reuse_continuation()` and the related review paths send Codex literal placeholder text instead of concrete retry context.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:64-84 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Post-render validation only checks the three legacy placeholders, so unresolved continuation placeholders are not detected.
  WHY: The renderer can exit successfully while still emitting literal `{{VAR}}` tokens, so broken continuation prompts reach Codex without an error.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:79-116 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `render_conflict_thread_reuse_continuation()` passes the retry-context values to `bash "${render_prompt_script}"` as shell assignments that are not exported, so the renderer subprocess cannot see them.
  WHY: Even if placeholder substitution existed, the continuation prompt would still render without the attempt number, max attempts, failure kind, and violation counts.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:1731-1844 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The retry/continuation rendering block can proceed with a continuation prompt that still contains unresolved placeholders instead of forcing a verified fallback to the full prompt.
  WHY: The failure is silent because the renderer can return success while leaving `{{VAR}}` tokens in place, so the retry path does not actually recover the intended context.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:1596-1598 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: `CONFLICT_RESOLVER_THREAD_REUSE_MARKER` is appended unconditionally even when thread reuse is disabled.
  WHY: This adds dead prompt text to the conflict-resolver prompt path, which is harmless but unnecessary and architecturally wrong.
- scripts/memory_helpers.sh:437-849 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Removing `memory_force_tick_get`, `memory_force_tick_put`, and their helper functions silently disables the force-tick cooldown/claim persistence path used by `scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh`.
  WHY: The `declare -F` guards now fail, so dispatches fall back to a no-op record and can race without the mutual-exclusion layer.
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:1266-1293 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The apply-fixes continuation path can also reach Codex with an unresolved continuation placeholder instead of a clean, smaller thread-reuse prompt.
  WHY: The same renderer/wiring path is used for the editor continuation, so the thread-reuse wrapper is fed a prompt that may still contain literal `{{SERENA_TOOL_HINTS}}` text.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:44 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The resolver-specific Serena hints are written from `SERENA_TOOL_HINTS`, but the caller exports `SERENA_TOOL_HINTS_RESOLVER`, so the resolver hints are never consumed.
  WHY: The `{{SERENA_TOOL_HINTS_RESOLVER}}` placeholder on the continuation prompt would remain unresolved even if the renderer handled the other variables.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

  confidence=5

  EVIDENCE: The continuation prompt files and contracts already exist, but the shell renderer cannot resolve the new continuation variables or inline placeholders, so the rendered prompts still contain literal `{{VAR}}` text.
- requirement: "Wire same-run thread reuse into the listed review/conflict shell entrypoints."
  expected_change_site: scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh and scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh
  confidence=4

  EVIDENCE: Structural wiring exists, but the runtime continuation render path is broken and unresolved placeholders reach Codex, so thread reuse is not usable.
- requirement: "Continuation prompts remain smaller than the original full prompt path."

  confidence=3

  EVIDENCE: The default-off gate is present, but `CONFLICT_RESOLVER_THREAD_REUSE_MARKER` is appended unconditionally and `scripts/memory_helpers.sh` force-tick helpers were removed unconditionally, so disabled runs are not fully behavior-preserving.

- requirement: "Scope: `prompts/mode-review-apply-fixes-continuation.txt`, `prompts/mode-review-conflict-resolver-continuation.txt`, `prompts/contracts/mode-review-apply-fixes-continuation.yml`, `prompts/contracts/mode-review-conflict-resolver-continuation.yml`, `scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh`, `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh`, `tests/test_codex_thread_reuse_review.py`"
  expected_change_site: scripts/render_prompt.sh
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:47-63 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The shell-based renderer only matches three legacy placeholders (`{{WORKFLOW_EDIT_RESTRICTION}}`, `{{SEMBLE_PREFETCH}}`, `{{SERENA_TOOL_HINTS}}`) as exact whole-line matches.
  WHY: The conflict-resolver continuation prompt contains eight new variables, including five inline placeholders like `Previous attempt: {{PREVIOUS_ATTEMPT_NUMBER}} of {{MAX_ATTEMPTS}}`, and they pass through unresolved into the prompt sent to Codex.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:44 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `SERENA_TOOL_HINTS_BLOCK="${SERENA_TOOL_HINTS:-}"` reads `SERENA_TOOL_HINTS`, but `render_conflict_thread_reuse_continuation()` exports `SERENA_TOOL_HINTS_RESOLVER`.
  WHY: The resolver-specific Serena hints are never consumed, so `{{SERENA_TOOL_HINTS_RESOLVER}}` remains unresolved.
- scripts/memory_helpers.sh:437-849 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The PR removes `memory_force_tick_get`, `memory_force_tick_put`, and four supporting helper functions.
  WHY: `scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh` depends on them behind `declare -F` guards, so the force-tick cooldown and claim-persistence path silently becomes a no-op.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:1596-1598 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: `CONFLICT_RESOLVER_THREAD_REUSE_MARKER="=== THREAD REUSE LIVE CONTEXT ==="` is unconditionally appended to `CONFLICT_RESOLVER_PROMPT_FILE`.
  WHY: When `conflict_thread_reuse_enabled` is false, the marker is still injected even though the wrapper is never installed.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:1831-1844 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: On retry, the code falls back to the full prompt path if `render_conflict_thread_reuse_continuation` fails, but the render call can succeed while still producing unresolved placeholders.
  WHY: Because `render_prompt.sh` exits 0 when it passes through unresolvable `{{VAR}}` tokens, the broken continuation prompt reaches Codex instead of the full prompt.

  Expected change site: The rendered continuation prompts as delivered to Codex via `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh` and `scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh`.
  Evidence of absence: The conflict-resolver continuation prompt contains eight `{{VAR}}` placeholders that the shell renderer cannot resolve, including inline placeholders that can never match the whole-line-only case statement.

  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- Requirement: "Add continuation prompts/contracts for review apply-fixes and review conflict resolution."

  Evidence of absence: The prompt template and contract files exist, but the shell renderer cannot resolve the new continuation variables, so the prompts are created without a working delivery path.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- Requirement: "Wire same-run thread reuse into the listed review/conflict shell entrypoints."
  Expected change site: `scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh` and `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh`.
  Evidence of absence: The wiring exists structurally, but the conflict-resolver continuation prompt reaches Codex with unresolved placeholders.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- Requirement: "Default-off fallback preserves current behavior."
  Expected change site: `scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh` and `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh`.
  Evidence of absence: The default-off gate exists, but `CONFLICT_RESOLVER_THREAD_REUSE_MARKER` is appended unconditionally and `scripts/memory_helpers.sh` had its force-tick functions removed unconditionally.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

  Evidence of absence: The PR modifies `scripts/memory_helpers.sh`, `scripts/render_prompt.sh`, and `scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py` outside the declared scope.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
